Subject: Benchmark measurement contract & prompt bundle — next steps

Hi Elena / Starlight team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth to move toward the pilot: 

Summary from the call:
- Scope: SLO qualification for the personalized-recommendation endpoint (streaming enabled)
- Primary metrics we agreed to evaluate: latency (p95 & p99), sustainable throughput at target concurrency, and streaming chunk tail latency for the interactive path.
- Goal: produce a reproducible benchmark that both teams can run and sign off on before pilot start.

Immediate asks / deliverables (Redwood):
1) Measurement contract (attached: SLO_measurement_contract_v1.xlsx) — defines metric formulas, warmup rules, sampling windows, and hardware baseline.
2) Prompt bundle and eval harness (attached: prompt_set_v1.tar.gz; eval-harness-readme.md) — includes prompt sets for single-turn and streaming scenarios, harness runbook, and a dockerized runner.
3) Reproducibility checklist — includes fixed random seeds, deterministic tokenization instructions, and environment capture steps.

Items we need from Starlight:
- Labeled sample set for 1k user sessions (anonymized) and a list of representative arrival patterns.
- Confirmation of target SLOs you care about (e.g., p99 <= 250ms single-turn, streaming chunk tail <= 80ms).
- Procurement timeline / any PO or compliance artifacts (SOC2, data residency requirements).

Proposed timeline:
- Redwood delivers measurement contract + harness + prompt bundle by 2027-06-23.
- Starlight provides sample data + procurement confirmation by 2027-06-24.
- Joint pilot run window: 2027-06-27 to 2027-06-30.

If this aligns I will: 1) share the Drive folder with the bundle, 2) open a HubSpot deal task (link below), and 3) drop a calendar invite for an alignment session to kick off the run.

Attachments: SLO_measurement_contract_v1.xlsx, prompt_set_v1.tar.gz, eval-harness-readme.md

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/67890
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPromptBundle

Thanks — I'll follow up with exact run commands and the docker image tag once the folder is shared.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Benchmark measurement contract & prompt bundle — next steps

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple of clarifying points from our side before we lock timelines: 

1) Latency targets: we typically qualify both p95 and p99. Our internal bar for single-turn interactive is p99 <= 200ms (at our baseline 8 concurrent sessions). Can Redwood provide both p95 and p99 in the contract?
2) Streaming semantics: our streaming path is incremental (partial tokens shown as they generate). For streaming SLOs we care about: (a) first-byte latency, (b) per-chunk tail (95/99) during steady-state streaming (>200 tokens), and (c) end-to-end completion time for the long-form path. Can the harness capture per-chunk timings?
3) Repro concerns: we require deterministic tokenization and fixed seeds where feasible. Also we need the ability to re-run the benchmark within our VPC; do you provide a self-hosted harness for private runs?

Procurement note: attached procurement_request.pdf — procurement will need SOC2-type evidence and an initial statement of data retention and encryption standards. We are aiming for a pilot start on 2027-07-01, but procurement may push for a week later depending on reviews.

Also a small ask: can Redwood confirm the hardware baseline you intend to use for the runs (GPU model, mem, OS/container image)? That should be explicit in the measurement contract.

Thanks — looking forward to the harness and prompt bundle.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Product Operations, Starlight Commerce
elena.park@starlight.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@starlight.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark measurement contract & prompt bundle — next steps

Elena — thanks for the specificity. I want to call out concrete measurement definitions so we are all aligned and the benchmark is reproducible whether run by Redwood or Starlight inside a private environment. Below are the key definitions I will bake into the contract and readme: 

Measurement definitions (draft):
- Single-turn latency (p95/p99): measured from request-send to final-token-emitted. For models with streaming enabled, we will also capture first-byte latency and the time between successive token-chunk emits.
- Streaming chunk tail latency: measure per-chunk latency distribution; report p95 and p99 on chunk emit intervals for runs longer than 200 tokens.
- Throughput / sustainable concurrency: defined as the highest QPS at which p99 single-turn stays below the agreed threshold for a 10-minute sustained window with autoscaling turned off.
- Warmup & cache rules: run a 300-sec warmup using the provided sample set; KV cache should be cold at run start unless explicitly requested otherwise; for runs that need cold-cache numbers we will include an additional cold-run protocol.
- Hardware baseline capture: each run must include a small environment manifest (GPU model, driver, container tag, CPU count, mem), and an engineered seed/config dump. We will include a docker image for the harness (sha256 tag in the readme).
- Arrival process: harness will support fixed concurrency, linear ramp, and Poisson arrivals. Please indicate which pattern matches your traffic for the pilot.

Reproducibility deliverables (what Redwood will provide):
- dockerized harness + run scripts (eval-harness-readme.md)
- prompt bundle with metadata and canonical seed file (prompt_set_v1.tar.gz)
- measurement contract spreadsheet (SLO_measurement_contract_v1.xlsx)

Answers to your direct questions: 
- Yes, harness captures per-chunk timings and will output a time-series of chunk emits for downstream analysis.
- Yes, we provide a self-hosted runner that can be executed inside your VPC; the docker image and a lightweight runner will be in the bundle.
- Hardware baseline for our hosted runs: NVIDIA A100 80GB (driver/ubuntu container details in the spreadsheet). We will label any runs done on lighter hardware so results are not confused.

Small request for Starlight: please indicate target concurrency and expected arrival pattern (e.g., Poisson with mean 8 rps per user). If you can share one anonymized log snippet we can mirror the pattern.

I will incorporate all of the above into version 1.1 of the contract and push to the Drive by EOD.

—
Neha Kapoor
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Elena —

Thanks — all sounds good. Quick confirmation of agreed deliverables and owners so we can close the loop: 

Agreed deliverables & owners:
- Redwood: deliver measurement contract v1.1, dockerized eval harness, and prompt bundle (owner: Neha). Delivery ETA: 2027-06-23.
- Starlight: provide anonymized 1k session sample + arrival pattern description; procurement confirmation on SOC2 and data retention (owner: Elena). ETA: 2027-06-24.
- Joint: schedule a 1-hour alignment session to pick the final SLO numbers and run the first paired benchmark. Proposed slot: 2027-06-25 10:00 AM PT — will send a calendar invite.

We will also include an explicit section in the contract describing hardware baseline and labeling rules (hosted vs. private) so results are comparable.

Follow-ups I will do today: share Drive folder, create HubSpot task, and send calendar invite for 6/25. Neha will push the harness docs and docker tag by EOD. Monica will coordinate access and onboarding details with your SRE if the run will be inside your VPC.

If you need any adjustments to dates, flag them and we will adapt. Otherwise I will assume the 6/23/6/24 cadence and proceed.

Cheers,
Karthik
